intended_object: The restriction map 𝒪_{x⁻¹} → 𝒪_{x,x⁻¹}, a k-algebra map. Here 𝒪_{x⁻¹} is the holomorphy ring of the places at which x⁻¹ is regular, and 𝒪_{x,x⁻¹} is the holomorphy ring of the places at which both x and x⁻¹ are regular, i.e. where x is a unit. Since both rings are subrings of F, this map is the inclusion. This reading comes from the docstring and the module documentation of the two-chart gluing.
explanation:
Holomorphy rings are antitone in the set of places. The set {P | x ∈ 𝒪_P} ∩ {P | x⁻¹ ∈ 𝒪_P} is contained in {P | x⁻¹ ∈ 𝒪_P}, so 𝒪_{x⁻¹} ⊆ 𝒪_{x,x⁻¹} as k-subalgebras of F. The definition is `Subalgebra.inclusion` applied to this containment, which is exactly the restriction of functions described in the docstring.

This map is one leg of the span Spec 𝒪_x ← Spec 𝒪_{x,x⁻¹} → Spec 𝒪_{x⁻¹}, i.e. one of the two open immersions in the gluing (Stichtenoth III.2; Hartshorne II.2.12).

The generality is right: the definition takes an arbitrary field extension F/k and an arbitrary x, and the function-field hypothesis is only added in the later results. It is a specific map, written with Mathlib's general `Subalgebra.inclusion` and not hand-built, so it is not too narrow. There is no separate Mathlib definition of this particular map, so `mathlib_counterpart` is left empty.

For x = 0 we get x⁻¹ = 0 and the map is still well defined; the gluing construction only uses it when x ≠ 0. Nothing is wrong in this degenerate case.
